description: About one in six people lives with a significant disability, and many more use a site one handed, in bright sun or with the text turned up. Most accessibility problems are not hard to fix. They are found late, when every fix means reworking a finished page.

title: Writing at work that people finish reading
summary: Write emails, updates and reports that get read, understood and acted on. Short lessons with before and after rewrites from real workplaces.
tagline: If the request is in paragraph four, nobody will find it.
description: Most workplace writing fails in the same few ways. The point arrives late, the sentences run long, and the reader has to work out what they are being asked to do. So they skim, miss the deadline and reply with a question the email already answered.
